remarks.name: Peter Yang
remarks.role: Practical AI tutorials and interviews for busy people
remarks.text:
Product manager = Member of product staff
Designer = Member of design staff
Engineer = Member of technical staff

Is this AI making job functions more verbose? 😅

If this flattens levels and titles, I'm all for it though.

It also shows that maybe the single AI builder title that combines all functions isn't really happening, even at the best labs. People still have specialties based on what they're good at.
remarks.translation: 产品经理 = 产品团队成员 设计师 = 设计团队成员 工程师 = 技术团队成员 这是AI让职位职能变得更冗长了吗？😅 不过，如果这能拉平层级和头衔，我完全支持。这也表明，也许那种将所有职能合而为一的单一AI构建者头衔并未真正实现，即使在最顶尖的实验室也是如此。人们仍然根据各自所长拥有专业分工。

remarks.name: Madhu Guru
remarks.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
remarks.text:
Every AI product should be working towards abstracting model choice away from users. 

In any product, the intelligence is the underlying engine - all the user cares about is that the job gets done. 

Model picking is too much cognitive load for the user.

There have been multiple attempts to abstract model choice away from users. I think we’re finally at the point where this can work well.

It takes three things:

1/ Deep understanding of the model frontier across different weight classes for your particular use cases.

2/ Great evals for your workflows, so you know which models work best where.

3/ A team with the talent and AI-native operating model to continuously adapt as the frontier moves.

Having worked with the Lovable team, I can say they have all three.
remarks.translation: 每个AI产品都应该致力于将模型选择从用户手中抽象出来。在任何产品中，智能都是底层引擎——用户只关心任务是否完成。挑选模型对用户来说认知负担太重了。已经有过多次尝试，想把模型选择从用户那里抽象掉。我认为我们终于到了这一步，这件事可以很好地实现了。这需要三样东西：1/ 针对你的特定用例，深入理解不同权重级别的模型前沿。2/ 为你的工作流建立出色的评估体系，这样你就能知道哪些模型在哪些场景下表现最好。3/ 一个拥有才华和AI原生运营模式的团队，能够随着前沿的推进持续适应。与Lovable团队共事过之后，我可以说他们三者兼备。
remarks.observation: 这条言论适合观察模型运行、算力、存储、sandbox 或开发平台基础设施的变化；后续事实判断需回到原始公告或技术文档。

podcasts.originalExcerpt: A few years ago, Caltech Prof. and co-founder of Accelerated Understanding, Anima Anandkumar set out to develop the first open-source weather model with AI. Talking to experts in the field, she was met with skepticism. Weather is chaotic, physics simulations are hard, have been developed for decades, and require supercomputers, the data just isn’t there. Despite reservations, Anima went forth and built. Within a year her team had developed FourCastNet, a predictive model that is competitive with the best physics-based simulations available. Thanks to Anima, and her follow up work, anyone can now predict weather accurately over a short timescale using consumer grade GPUs.
